title: Element symbols that come from old names
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Most element symbols match their English names: O for oxygen, C for carbon. A few do not, because they come from the old Latin names that chemists used when the symbols were set in the 1800s. These eleven trip people up, so they are worth learning on their own.

How to hold it: These are pairs (symbol and name) that don't look alike, which is exactly where a mnemonic earns its keep. Make each pair into one vivid picture that holds both, like the hooks below, then test yourself from both sides: symbol to name and name to symbol. Saying the old name out loud ("aurum") is the bridge between the two.
